paper.title_en: Zone-folded Goldstone mode of the field-induced spin supersolid in the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet
paper.abstract_en: The field-induced spin supersolid of the square-lattice $S=1$ antiferromagnet with single-ion and exchange anisotropy has so far been characterized only by static observables, among them a two-peak transverse structure factor. We compute its dynamic spin structure factors, and those of the neighboring phases, by stochastic analytic continuation of stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo data on a $16\times16$ lattice at inverse temperature $β=32$, at one field in each of the supersolid, the $m_z=1/2$ Ising plateau and the canted $XY$ phase. The supersolid has a single Goldstone mode, which the checkerboard folds onto both the ordering wave vector $\mathbf{Q}=(π,π)$ and $\mathbf{q}=(0,0)$, so that it appears in both spin channels at both points with one velocity $v=1.36\pm0.01$. The canted phase shows half of this pattern and the plateau none, the latter carrying instead a gapped magnon band and a two-magnon longitudinal continuum. Exactly at $\mathbf{Q}$ and $(0,0)$ the finite-lattice spectra are governed by a rotor tower of the condensate in the transverse channel and an Ising doublet of the checkerboard in the longitudinal one, both present at $\mathbf{Q}$ in the supersolid. Three parameter-free comparisons with the stiffness and the uniform susceptibility of the same runs, for the velocity, the sound-mode weight and the thermal decay of the rotor tower, tie the continued spectra to raw Monte Carlo observables. The folded Goldstone mode is the dynamical fingerprint of the supersolid.
